lines.text: You type a question and press Enter.
Less than a second later, an answer starts to appear. But what happened in that second?
First, your words are chopped into small pieces, called tokens.
To the AI, each token is just a list of numbers.
These numbers rush into a giant web of artificial neurons.
A big open model has about seventy billion parameters, and for every token, it uses all of them.
That's around a hundred and forty billion calculations. For one token.
All this math runs on chips like this one. A GPU.
They run so hot that thousands of them live in huge buildings, full of cooling pipes and power lines.
And then, out comes the answer. Not all of it. Just one token.
And the whole thing starts again. For every. Single. Word.
So the next time you say thank you to a chatbot, somewhere, a building gets a little warmer.
